transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-22 09:15 UTC | Duration: 52 min | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Lena (Boreal Head of Compliance), Priya (Boreal CISO), Marcus (Boreal DevOps)

Summary: quick posture readout for SOC 2 / ISO27001, confirm what evidence Boreal needs, and plan technical follow-ups for RBAC/SSO and KMS.

[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Can you hear me okay?
[00:06] Lena: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks, Samira.
[00:08] Samira: Great. Quick intros — I'm Samira with Redwood, AE. Daniel's our systems engineer, he'll do the technical bits. Over to you all?
[00:15] Priya: Hi, I'm Priya, CISO at Boreal. We're here to validate controls mapping for an external audit and see how Redwood will provide evidence and access.
[00:24] Marcus: Marcus, DevOps, I'll look after the integration stuff.
[00:28] Daniel: Thanks, team. We'll walk through our Trust Center options and the KMS flow. I may ask to share screens later.
[00:36] Samira: Quick agenda: SOC2 artifacts, trust center access levels, RBAC/SSO approach, audit logs and retention, encryption/KMS, then action items. Anything to add?
[00:45] Lena: Please highlight how audit logs look — auditors care about schema, retention and tamper evidence.
[00:51] Samira: Noted.

[02:12] Daniel: To start, Redwood offers a read-only Trust Center workspace we can grant to auditor emails. It contains our SOC 2 Type II report, ISO27001 scope summary, and a controls mapping CSV. The tenant-level access is via SSO and we also support time-limited shared links.
[02:30] Priya: Time-limited links — are those link-based or do they require user auth? Our security policy prefers authenticated access only.
[02:38] Daniel: Authenticated only by default. The share link can be set to require the auditor to log in via SAML or we can provision a read-only user with RBAC.
[02:49] Marcus: How do you manage audit trail for when the auditor views evidence? Need an access log vendor side.
[02:55] Daniel: Yes, Trust Center records auditor access events and includes timestamp, actor, IP, and object accessed. We can export that as a CSV or push to your syslog endpoint.

[04:10] Samira: Lena, from a compliance perspective, what is your must-have list?
[04:14] Lena: SOC2 Type II report, the control mapping to our internal control IDs, encryption evidence for data-at-rest, KMS key rotation policy, audit log retention policy, and proof of encrypted backups. Also vendor contracts and subprocessors list.
[04:28] Samira: Got it. We'll make sure those items are surfaced.

[06:00] Daniel: On RBAC and SSO — Redwood supports SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning. Two common patterns: 1) Map IdP groups to Redwood roles (recommended for enterprises). 2) Service accounts for auditors with scoped read-only roles. Both support session expiry and enforced MFA.
[06:22] Priya: For us group-to-role mapping is preferred. Can you do group attribute mapping for nested groups? Our IdP uses nested groups in SAML assertions.
[06:30] Daniel: We can consume group attributes and support nested group flattening, though sometimes the assertion size hits limits. If that happens we use SCIM for provisioning.
[06:42] Marcus: SCIM — what's the latency for provisioning changes? We're concerned about on-call rotations.
[06:47] Daniel: Typical SCIM sync is near real-time, within a minute for single updates; bulk changes might take longer.

[08:10] Lena: On RBAC, auditors want to see role definitions and last change timestamp. Do you keep historical role-change records?
[08:17] Daniel: Yes, role-change events are logged and immutable within the Trust Center audit index. We retain those logs per your retention policy; default is 365 days but it's configurable.

[10:05] Marcus: Data residency — we have constraints: PHI must stay in us-east-1 and EU staff data in eu-west-1. Can Redwood pin tenancy/region for a specific tenant?
[10:16] Daniel: For Redwood Private and Dedicated customers we can pin model serving to regions. For hosted we support region tenancy on request and can ensure data storage and logs remain in the selected region. We'll capture the exact region list you need.

[12:00] Samira: Quick note on encryption/KMS — we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) in major clouds and HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. Daniel, maybe walk through the KMS flow?
[12:12] Daniel: Sure. Top-level: customer holds KMS key (or we can hold it managed) — Redwood encrypts at rest with envelope encryption. The workflow: data encrypted with a DEK (data encryption key), which is encrypted with the CMK. For HSM customers, key wrap is FIPS 140-2 validated. Key rotation is supported and we store rotation metadata in the Trust Center.
[12:38] Priya: If we hold the CMK does Redwood retain any unencrypted snapshot?
[12:44] Daniel: No, not in normal flows. We never store plaintext. The only time plaintext appears briefly is in-memory during processing and we zero memory via secure allocator. The audit logs show KMS decrypt events with cryptographic material never persisted.

[14:20] Lena: Auditors will ask about key rotation cadence and proof. Can you provide a rotation ledger or report?
[14:26] Daniel: Yes, we can export key rotation history with timestamps, algorithm, and who initiated rotation. We'll prepare a short diagram and sample export.

[16:50] Marcus: About audit logs — format and export. Our auditors expect JSON Lines with certain fields: timestamp, actor_id, action, object_type, object_id, request_id, ip, region, and integrity hash. Can you output that?
[17:02] Daniel: Yes, we support JSONL export including a SHA256 integrity hash for each line if you want tamper-evidence; plus request_id and kv-cache identifiers. Note, sometimes model-related fields get truncated when tokenized so we'll include full request payload in a separate secure artifact when required.

[19:30] Samira: Retention defaults?
[19:33] Daniel: Default log retention is 1 year; we can extend to 7 years for enterprise contracts. We also support export to your long-term archive like S3 with server-side encryption supplied by your KMS.

[21:45] Priya: For ISO27001 evidence mapping, do you have a controls mapping template we can align to our ISMS control IDs?
[21:54] Daniel: Yes. We maintain a controls mapping CSV that maps Redwood controls to SOC2 criteria and ISO27001 Annex A controls. We'll share the template and we can pre-populate common mappings.

[24:10] Lena: A couple of gotchas we've seen: vendors sometimes have read-only Trust Center but admins copy artifacts into shared drives. We need chain-of-custody notes. How do you handle exported evidence?
[24:23] Daniel: Exports are tagged with provenance metadata: who exported, when, and destination. We also can limit export to auditor accounts only. Exports can be digitally signed.

[26:05] Marcus: Integration touchpoints — SSO, SCIM for users, syslog/HTTPS for logs, and a KMS endpoint. Any other connectors?
[26:13] Daniel: We also support SIEM forwarders, GCP Stackdriver, Azure Monitor, and webhooks for critical events.

[28:00] Samira: Timeline question — Boreal's audit kickoff is early Sept. What would a minimal pilot look like to get the auditors the artifacts?
[28:12] Daniel: Minimal pilot: read-only Trust Center + sample audit log export + KMS rotation ledger. That gives auditors the high-level artifacts, and then we follow with a deep-dive session. We can deliver those artifacts within 7 business days after access is granted.

[30:40] Priya: For the pilot we want to control the auditor access window to two weeks. Can we do time-boxed RBAC?
[30:47] Daniel: Yes, we can provision temporary auditor roles with auto-expiry and require MFA. We'll document the exact steps.

[32:05] Lena: On the controls mapping CSV, can you include our internal control IDs and status columns (implemented / partial / planned)?
[32:12] Daniel: Absolutely. We'll pre-fill implemented controls and leave blank columns for your team to fill status and evidence references.

[34:20] Samira: Any licensing or pricing items tied to Trust Center or extra audit exports?
[34:27] Samira: Quick answer: read-only Trust Center access for auditors is included; extended retention and private KMS/HSM have add-on pricing — we'll follow up in the quote.

[36:10] Marcus: A question on VPC peering and private deployments: if we go Dedicated, can we keep inference nodes in a customer VPC?
[36:18] Daniel: For Dedicated and Private, yes. We support VPC peering and on-prem options — network isolation is full.

[38:05] Priya: Anything about backups — are backups encrypted with the same CMK?
[38:10] Daniel: Yes, backups are encrypted with DEKs wrapped by CMKs. We can show backup metadata and retention policies.

[40:00] Lena: For the audit evidence package, auditors often want chain-of-custody — can you sign the package and provide a hash?
[40:07] Daniel: Yes, export packages are signed and we provide a SHA256 manifest.

[42:30] Samira: Ok, let's recap next steps. Samira will send the SOC2 Type II PDF and Trust Center read-only link. Daniel to share sample audit log JSONL and KMS rotation diagram. Boreal to confirm data residency regions and auditor contact. We'll schedule a 30-min technical deep dive for RBAC/SSO next week.

[44:00] Priya: Sounds good. A small nit: in the docs reference 'KV cache' sometimes shows as 'k-v cache' or 'kv caching' — auditors might not like inconsistent naming. Could you standardize wording in the controls mapping?
[44:12] Daniel: Good catch — we'll standardize the terminology and include a glossary in the controls mapping CSV.

[46:55] Marcus: For the syslog forwarder, what's the recommended encryption? TLS mutual auth?
[47:02] Daniel: mTLS is recommended. We support TLS 1.2+ and client certs for additional auth.

[49:30] Lena: Anything else?
[49:32] Priya: No, I think we covered the main ask.
[49:35] Samira: Great, thanks everyone. We'll send meeting notes and the artifacts.
[50:00] (crosstalk and meeting wrap)

End of transcript.
